findings.checklist_item: Define the non-memoization predicate against how the allowlisted tools actually signal errors (string returns like 'Error: ...' / resolver 'UNRESOLVED', not raised exceptions), and reconcile whether '(no matches)' should be memoized (deterministic) or exempted — the tools in pai_tools.py never raise into the agent loop.
evidence: Plan: 'Error results are NEVER memoized: a failed call passes through on retry (legitimate retries must re-execute).'
AC4: 'a call that raised re-executes on the next identical call'
pai_tools.py:56/61/81/85/108/145 return `f"Error: {exc}"` (never raise); :165 returns '(no matches)'; show_ticket :255 catches Exception and returns a string
Context cites 'another looped 62x on an honest "(no matches)" result' — a non-raising string return the exception-based predicate cannot classify
findings.finding: The plan's error-non-memoization mechanism keys on RAISED exceptions, but all four allowlisted read-only tools signal errors as ordinary string returns and never raise into the agent loop, so transient errors and honest '(no matches)' results would be memoized against the plan's intent.
findings.location: Approach / AC line 'Error results are not memoized: a call that raised re-executes'
scenarios: A read_file hits a transient OSError, returns 'Error: ...' as a string; the memo caches it and re-serves the stale error on every identical retry instead of re-executing
search_files returns '(no matches)' from a transient miss; memo pins it
findings.suggested_fix: Detect error results by return-value shape (e.g. leading 'Error:' from the fs tools) rather than by exception, and state explicitly whether a deterministic '(no matches)' is memoized-with-nudge (correct dedup) or exempted; update AC4 to test the string-error passthrough path, since a counting-stub that raises will not exercise real tool behavior.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define (or defer) the manifest contract the FULL/skeleton branch reads — its accessor/shape and the FULL vs skeleton marker vocabulary — so the memo wrapper and AC line 6's FULL-manifest test have a concrete interface; if it must wait for the sibling, move the FULL-branch AC behind that dependency rather than requiring it now.
evidence: Repo search for 'manifest'/'skeleton'/'preload' finds NO pre-loading file manifest with FULL/skeleton markers; the only 'manifest' hits are attestation/signing manifests, unrelated
Plan: 'Manifest absent (this ticket ships before the pre-loading sibling)' — confirms the producing sibling has not landed
AC line 6: 'with a manifest marking a file FULL the nudge says already-in-context' requires exercising the FULL branch, but no manifest schema/marker enum is defined to build the fixture

T8(a)/(b): a schema (the manifest) and its marker vocabulary (FULL vs skeleton) are referenced by the memo wrapper and by a mandated test but never defined co-located with the consumer that needs them
findings.finding: The in-context nudge branch and AC line 6 depend on a pre-loading sibling's 'manifest' with FULL/skeleton file markers, but neither the plan nor the repo defines that manifest's shape, the FULL/skeleton marker vocabulary, or the API by which the memo wrapper reads it — and the plan states this ticket ships before the sibling. AC line 6 nonetheless mandates a unit test 'with a manifest marking a file FULL', which is unconstructable without a defined manifest type.
findings.location: Approach section ('In-context nudge for pre-loaded files: when the pre-loading sibling's manifest marks a file FULL...') + AC line 6
scenarios: The executor writing the AC-6 FULL-manifest test has no manifest type to instantiate, so the test either invents an ad-hoc shape that later drifts from the sibling's real manifest or the FULL branch ships untested
The memo wrapper's manifest-read code path is written against a guessed interface that the sibling later contradicts
findings.suggested_fix: Either specify a minimal manifest-lookup seam this ticket owns (e.g. a callable returning a per-path marker from {FULL, skeleton}) that the sibling later populates, or restate AC line 6 as manifest-absent-only for this ticket and defer the FULL-branch test to the pre-loading sibling.

findings.checklist_item: Specify the memo/steering precedence past tool_step_limit: state whether a cache hit is still superseded by the steering notice once run_step > limit, and confirm the steering notice string is never itself memoized.
evidence: agent_call.py:59-62 steering returns TOOL_STEP_STEERING_NOTICE when ctx.run_step > limit
With memo outside steering, a cache hit returns before steering's run_step check runs

Plan does not address whether a cached hit should still be superseded by the steering notice past the limit, nor whether a post-limit steering NOTICE (a non-error string) could itself be cached on first occurrence
findings.finding: The memo wrapper sits outside the steering boundary (guard->memo->steering), so a signature whose first execution was cached can be served the cached real result after the tool_step_limit is crossed, bypassing the steering convergence notice; the plan does not specify this interaction.
findings.location: Approach: 'wrapper order runaway guard OUTERMOST -> memo -> steering'
scenarios: Model repeats an allowlisted call after the tool_step_limit; memo serves the cached body+nudge instead of the 'produce your final answer now' steering notice
A signature first seen AFTER the limit returns the steering notice; memo caches the notice as if it were a result

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the verbatim text (or a concrete template with its filled example) of the level-1, level-2, and manifest-FULL in-context nudge messages, the way TOOL_STEP_STEERING_NOTICE is authored inline.
evidence: Plan: 'a static templated nudge line ... a stronger static nudge' names three distinct message levels but supplies no exemplar string
Existing sibling TOOL_STEP_STEERING_NOTICE at agent_call.py:38 defines the analogous steering-notice text verbatim inline
T8(a): an LLM-consumed surface (the nudge messages) whose content vocabulary is referenced but never defined — the wording is what actually steers the model, so it is load-bearing
findings.finding: The three LLM-facing nudge messages (level-1 repeat nudge, level-2 stronger nudge, and the manifest-FULL 'already in context above' nudge) are the steering content of this feature, yet the plan never states their actual text — only that they are 'static templated' and 'byte-stable'. The sibling steering surface in the same module (TOOL_STEP_STEERING_NOTICE, agent_call.py:38) gives its full wording inline; these nudges do not.
findings.location: Approach section ('first repeat... static templated nudge line; further repeats... stronger static nudge') + AC line 2 ('first repeat carries the level-1 static nudge, subsequent repeats the level-2 text')
scenarios: An executor implements the nudges with wording that does not actually redirect the model, defeating the 'nudge-then-abort' goal while still passing the byte-stability AC
AC line 2's test can assert byte-stability but has no authored text to pin, so two implementations diverge on the steering content
findings.suggested_fix: Author the three nudge strings inline in the plan (e.g. as named constants), each including the cached tool name/signature template slot, so their wording is reviewable and the byte-stability AC pins real text.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the memo cache's lifecycle: it is created per agent-call arming and retired when that call completes (same scope as the runaway-guard window), so no signature is cached across independent runs.
evidence: Plan states the key ('the EXISTING usage_log tool-call signature') and that errors are never memoized, but never states the cache's CREATE/RETIRE scope — whether it is instantiated and torn down per agent_call arming or persists.
The runaway guard is described as windowed per-call state (agent_call.py); the memo cache scope is left implicit.
findings.finding: The memo cache's lifecycle scope and retirement are unstated: the plan defines the cache KEY (usage_log signature) but not whether the cache is per-agent-call, per-run, or process-global, nor when it is cleared. If the cache outlives a single agent call it could serve a stale cached read-only result across an unrelated later call (e.g. a file re-read after an intervening write by a sibling tool in another run) or leak/accumulate across runs.
findings.location: Approach / 'Key: the EXISTING usage_log tool-call signature'
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to Approach fixing the cache scope to a single agent_call invocation (constructed when the wrapper is armed, discarded at call end), matching the actuator's per-call windowing; add a unit assertion that a fresh wrapper starts with an empty cache.
